args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, health checks started failing in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Error rate was 18%. v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. We rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions are running v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 (the latest deploy) was unhealthy in production in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate. Its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy in staging. I rolled all three regions back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that had been healthy in production. No approval was needed because v2.3.0 had been healthy before.
- **Result:** All regions are now on v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001, titled "checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0". It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery. The incident's next step is to find out why v2.3.1 failed before redeploying it. The first attempt to create it was rate-limited, so I retried with the same idempotency key. Only one incident was created.
